new_statements.quote: 11. Le schème tonal des verbes gbayi a été déterminé dans le cadre : sujet wō 'il' + verbe ± complément + zí ndɛ̄ (marques aspectuelles). On observe trois classes tonales principales : B (cv̀, cv̀cv̀) M (cv̄) HB (cv̂, cv́₁v̀₁/cv́₁v̀₂, cv́cv̀) [...] 12. Le ton haut a une fonction dans la conjugaison verbale comme marque d'un aspect actuel : ainsi, cv̀, cv̄, cv̂ se neutralisent en cv́ dans cet aspect [...] 13. On observe les schèmes tonals nominaux suivants : B (cv̀, cv̀cv̀, cv̀cv̀cv̀) M (cv̄, cv̄cv̄) H (cv́) HM [...] HB [...] BM [...] BH [...] MB [...] MH [...]
new_statements.translation: 11. The tonal scheme of Gbayi verbs was determined in the frame: subject wō 'he' + verb ± complement + zí ndɛ̄ (aspect markers). Three main tonal classes are observed: L (cv̀, cv̀cv̀), M (cv̄), HL (cv̂, cv́v̀, cv́cv̀) [...] 12. High tone has a function in verbal conjugation as the marker of a 'present/actual' aspect: cv̀, cv̄, cv̂ neutralise to cv́ in this aspect [...] 13. The following nominal tonal schemes are observed: L, M, H, HM, HL, LM, LH, ML, MH [...]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Gbayi is described as a three-register tone language (Low/Mid/High plus contour HB/MB) with lexical tone schemes on verbs and nouns and a grammatical High tone; the description says nothing at all about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tonal notes only: CV nouns cannot bear a lexical contour (unlike Yakoma); nouns with non-low final tone tend to take a final falling contour (HB/MB) at the end of a noun phrase (§14); some B/M nouns raise their final tone to H as N1 of an associative construction (§13).
new_statements.domain_note: Tone schemes elicited in a sentence frame (subject pronoun + verb ± complement + aspect particles); §14 contour is NP-final (phrase-level). No word-level prominence discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Boyd 1988 describes the Ngbandic language whose speakers call themselves gbāyī [gbʌ̄yī] and are called 'Kpatiri' by neighbours (Mingala sub-prefecture, Kotto river, CAR); data from two schoolboy speakers born in Mingala, recorded at Alindao in Feb 1985. This is Glottolog gbay1278 / ISO gyg. Not to be confused with Kpatili (ISO kpm, Zande group, 'langue proche du nzakara'), which Boyd's added HAL comments explicitly distinguish.

sources.note: Nothing. Sections 5-10 give segmental phonology (consonants, 7 vowels, vowel co-occurrence), sections 11-14 describe tone: three registers (B/M/H), verbal tone classes B, M, HB, nominal schemes B, M, H, HM, HB, BM, BH, MB, MH, grammatical H tone for 'aspect actuel', phrase-final contour tones. No mention of accent, stress or intensity anywhere (grep accent/intensité/stress/proéminence = 0 hits).
